title: The Detention of Maple Street
premise: Isandro Galloway has perfected the art of being unseen—until a mysterious group chat called Detention begins sending them messages about events before they happen, each prediction tied to something the school board buried years ago: the closure of Maple Street's community center and the students it quietly failed. As Isandro and four other 'invisibles' follow the chat's breadcrumbs through old yearbooks, sealed records, and their own families' pasts, they discover the predictions are coming from someone who was there—and someone who won't survive to see the truth told unless they act. In the end, Isandro must choose between staying safe and invisible or standing in front of the school board with the evidence, exposing the cover-up at the cost of their own carefully guarded anonymity.
about_author: Lena Marchetti grew up above her family's bakery in a rust-belt town where the community center closed the summer she turned fourteen. She writes stories about kids who find their people in the unlikeliest rooms, and she still believes bread can hold a feeling.

chapters.title: The Recipe for Invisible
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. We meet Isandro in the family bakery at 5 a.m., kneading worry into sourdough before school, mapping the hallways of Northgate High like a baker maps proofing times—everything measured, nothing felt. A flashback shows why invisibility became survival after middle school. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: First Notice
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. An unknown number adds Isandro to a group chat called 'Detention' with four strangers from school. The first message predicts the fountain will flood by Friday. Isandro ignores it—until Thursday, when the fountain erupts and floods the gym. Emotional beat: unease curdling into fascination.

chapters.title: The Other Four
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs introduce the chat members: Priya, the debate star who fakes certainty; Marcus, the janitor's son; Wren, a selective mute artist; and Theo, the expelled kid nobody talks to. Each got a different first prediction. Emotional beat: five loners realizing they were chosen on purpose.

chapters.title: Proofing
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The group meets secretly in the bakery after hours. Isandro brings bread shaped like an apology no one asked for. They test the chat with a controlled experiment—a prediction about the vending machines—that comes true exactly. Emotional beat: skeptical camaraderie, the first spark of belonging.

chapters.title: What the Board Buried
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. A new prediction references 'the Maple Street file.' Marcus recognizes the address—the community center his father helped close in 2019. Digging through his dad's work keys, he finds a locked storage room under the old gym. Emotional beat: loyalty to family colliding with hunger for truth.

chapters.title: Wren Sees Everything
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren communicates through sketchbook pages, revealing drawings made weeks ago that match the chat's predictions exactly—which means either Wren is the source, or someone is watching Wren. The group fractures over suspicion. Emotional beat: the pain of being doubted by your first real friends.

chapters.title: Detention, Literally
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. All five get Saturday detention on fabricated charges—someone with admin access is watching them back. Vice Principal Kessler interrogates them individually, asking oddly specific questions about Maple Street. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: The Yearbook Gap
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. In the library archive, Isandro discovers the 2019 yearbook is missing its final twenty pages—the spring the center closed. A librarian's trembling hint points to a student who transferred away that June. Emotional beat: the thrill of a real lead, and dread of what it costs.

chapters.title: Bread and Confessions
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro bakes panic into a batch of rolls and finally tells Priya the truth: Isandro's mother was the center's last director, fired and silenced, which is why the Galloways keep their heads down. Priya shares her own secret. Emotional beat: vulnerability as the price of trust.

chapters.title: The Prediction That Fails
chapters.summary: Group POV rotation. For the first time, a prediction doesn't come true—a fire alarm scheduled to go off never does. Relief turns to horror when they realize the chat changed because THEY changed something. The source isn't predicting the future; it's negotiating with it. Emotional beat: agency dawning, terrifying and exhilarating.

chapters.title: Kessler's Office
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya baits Kessler with a fake lead and records him shredding a document labeled MAPLE ST — FINAL. They now know the board knew. But the recording device goes missing afterward. Emotional beat: victory soured by the sense of being one step behind.

chapters.title: The Kid Who Transferred
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo tracks down the transferred student: Jesse Okafor, now living two towns over, who was in the center's afterschool program the night of 'the incident' the board covered up—an injury, a hushed settlement, five names redacted. Jesse refuses to talk but slips Theo a key. Emotional beat: grief for a childhood the town erased.

chapters.title: Locked Room, Open Wound
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. The key opens the storage room under the old gym: boxes of records, a damaged wheelchair, and incident reports naming Kessler and three board members. Marcus photographs everything as alarms trigger overhead. Emotional beat: triumph interrupted by the trap snapping shut.

chapters.title: Scattered
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The five scatter as security sweeps the building. Wren hides in the dark among the boxes and finds a photo of themselves at age nine—in the center's program. Wren was there too; the memory was taken along with the words. Emotional beat: devastating recognition, identity cracking open.

chapters.title: The Chat Goes Silent
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Detention sends one final message: 'Friday. Board meeting. Or I stop talking forever.' Then nothing. The group realizes the source is a student still inside Northgate, running out of time—possibly literally, given the medical records in the boxes. Emotional beat: urgency replacing fear.

chapters.title: Suspects and Sourdough
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The group narrows suspects using what only an insider would know, while Isandro caters the faculty luncheon and eavesdrops. A custodial aide, Ms. Ferro, hums the same tune from a video in the evidence boxes. Emotional beat: detective-work warmth, found family functioning as one organism.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Greenhouse
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. They corner Ms. Ferro—or rather, she lets them find her. She's Jesse's older sister, hired at Northgate to watch the board, feeding the chat through the school's ancient messaging system. But she didn't send the last message. Someone else has access. Emotional beat: alliance formed, new threat revealed.

chapters.title: Kessler's Counterstrike
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Kessler suspends all five, threatens expulsion, and has the storage room emptied overnight. Isandro's mother, seeing her child fight the fight she surrendered, hands Isandro her own hidden copy of the original incident report. Emotional beat: generational healing; the parent finally standing behind the kid.

chapters.title: Twenty-Two Hours
chapters.summary: Group POV rotation. With suspension papers pending and the board meeting Friday night, the five split tasks: Priya preps testimony, Marcus copies files to the cloud, Wren paints a mural-sized timeline in the courtyard overnight, Theo convinces Jesse to come, and Isandro bakes 300 rolls stamped with the center's logo. Emotional beat: exhausted, hopeful momentum.

chapters.title: The Meeting
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Climax. At the packed board meeting, Kessler moves to expel them before they speak—but Wren stands and speaks aloud for the first time in six years, presenting the mural photos. Jesse testifies. The final chat message appears on the auditorium screen, sent live from inside the room: the source is Kessler's own assistant, the fifth redacted name, forcing the vote. Emotional beat: courage at full volume.

chapters.title: Aftertaste
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Fallout and repair: Kessler resigns under investigation, the district votes to reopen the Maple Street center, and the five face a week of consequences they wear like medals. Isandro's parents host a reopening fundraiser at the bakery. Emotional beat: tender exhaustion, the strange lightness of being seen.

chapters.title: Open Sign
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Epilogue, months later. The reopened center's kitchen hosts a teen baking class Isandro teaches; the group chat renames itself 'Recess.' Isandro bakes a loaf with no feelings hidden inside—for the first time, nothing needs burying. Final line echoes chapter one's recipe, rewritten. Emotional beat: belonging, fully risen.
